annotations.title: Find where AI answers come from

description: WHERE AI ANSWERS ABOUT YOUR CATEGORY ACTUALLY COME FROM, and whether you are really on those pages. Walks your recent scans and rolls up every third-party host the seven engines cited when answering your tracked prompts: how often it was cited, which rival brands the engines associate with it, which of your prompts it answers, and sample URLs. Then — the field that matters most — `youOnThisSite`, which is not inferred from the answers but comes from OPENING those pages and reading them: 'absent' means we read the page in full and your brand is not on it (that is the citation gap, `isGap: true`), 'mentioned' means you are named with no link back, 'linked' means the page links to you, 'unreachable' means the site refused an automated read, and 'unknown' means it has not been read yet. The last two are NOT evidence of absence and must never be reported as gaps. Pass `search` by brand name, host or URL fragment to answer which page or site a brand is and how many citations it has. Search returns `pages`, including rival-owned and other excluded pages; `excludedAs` says why a page is not a pitch target. Rival-owned and engine-owned domains are excluded from `targets`, because a mention on a competitor's own blog or in a search vendor's docs is not an opportunity. Also returns `yourPagesEnginesCite`, the pages of yours engines DO cite, so you can see what is already working: up to 50, most-cited first, each with its citation `count` and per-engine `byEngine`. Fewer than 50 means the list is complete, so a page of yours that is missing had no citations in the range; at 50 it may have been cut. `whatEachEngineReads` gives, per engine, how many answers cited you and the sites it leans on most. Pass `engine` to rank the targets for one engine's answers only (e.g. what Perplexity reads that ChatGPT does not). This is usually the highest-leverage list in the product and the one that explains a citation score that will not move: improving your own page is a different job from being present in the pages engines already read. Free, reads stored scan and page-check data. Requires a signed-in account.

engine.description: Optional. Count targets and your cited pages from ONE engine's answers: chatgpt, perplexity, gemini, claude, grok, aioverviews (Google AI Overviews) or aimode (Google AI Mode). Omit for every engine. `whatEachEngineReads` always covers all of them.

gapsOnly.description: Only VERIFIED gaps — hosts whose cited pages we read in full and your brand was not on them (`youOnThisSite: 'absent'`). Excludes hosts not yet read, so this can under-report early on. Default false, which returns every target ranked gaps-first.

limit.description: Max targets and, with search, pages returned (1-100 each). Default 25. `totalTargets` counts every candidate host before this cut, so fewer targets than that means the list was truncated.

offset.description: Skip this many targets, to page past the first `limit`: pass the `nextOffset` the previous call returned until it comes back null. Pages follow the citation ranking and never overlap. Default 0.

range.description: The same window as the app's Sources screen. The API defaults to 30d.

search.description: Find cited pages by brand name, host or URL fragment, e.g. marqeable or marqeable.com/blog.

name: list_citation_sources
